method: camera traps at semi-arboreal (2-5 m) and terrestrial (40 cm) heights; activity pattern analysis of margay records
conditions: Wild margays in a privately protected area in Las Piedras, Madre de Dios, Peru (Hoja Nueva research station); the 2022 survey deployed camera traps at 62 sites over 80 nights in two grids (grid A, 33 sites, July to September 2022; grid B, 29 sites, September to November 2022), at semi-arboreal (2-5 m) and terrestrial (40 cm) heights. Methods (Activity patterns): 'camera trap data from 64 distinct margay captures were analyzed'; the paper does not say which grids, years or camera heights the 64 captures come from, and the activity analysis does not separate camera heights. Results: the activity analysis 'based on 64 records' gave distinct nocturnal peaks at 12 am to 3 am and 5 am and 'notably at 6 pm' (Figure 5); the Results elsewhere give '23 out of the total 47 detections were semi-arboreal', and the 64 and the 47 are not reconciled in the text. The Discussion calls the activity 'predominantly nocturnal'; no percentage of records at night is reported. Overlap with sympatric ocelot Dhat4 = 0.79 (bootstrap CI 0.706 to 0.909) and with jaguarundi Dhat1 = 0.21 (n = 3 jaguarundi, CI 0.013 to 0.413, called inconclusive); an expanded eight-grid dataset (293 sites, 2015-2022; 147 margay, 1,249 ocelot, 40 jaguarundi captures) raised these to 0.88 and 0.35, which the authors call likely more accurate (other species, not filed). The Methods mention no bait, lure or attractant; stations were placed away from human trails, terrestrial cameras ideally on mammal trails.

source.authors: Zwicker S, Sánchez-Latorre C, Lukasser C
source.title: Increasing detections of the margay: occupancy, density, and activity patterns in Madre de Dios, Peru

quote: Activity pattern analyses indicated primary nocturnal behavior with peaks at midnight to 3 am, 5 am, and 6 pm.
